I am a 51-year-old woman who has farmed these fields in Quzhou for over three decades. My family has about 6 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and follow the county extension leaflets, but at the end of the day I trust what I have seen with my own eyes and what my neighbors do. 

This year, I will stick to the winter wheat–summer maize double crop on all 6 mu. That is the backbone of our county. The soil is fertile loam, the irrigation wells work, and the buyers come right to the village for both grains. I thought about planting a mu of greenhouse vegetables for extra cash, but the market is too unpredictable and my back is not what it used to be, so I will stay with grain. For wheat, I will buy an improved variety seed from the local supply store—something like Jimai or Luneng series that yields well and resists lodging. For maize, I will use a hybrid seed; the price is higher, but the yield jump is too big to ignore. 

I will rotary-till the wheat field before sowing in mid-October to break up the stubble and bury the base fertilizer. For the summer maize, I will plant right after the wheat harvest in early June with no-tillage to save time and diesel—everyone here does that now because the window between crops is only about ten days. 

Fertilizer: for wheat, I will put down about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu total, split between base dressing and two top-dressings at green-up and jointing, plus roughly 6 kg of phosphorus and 5 kg of potassium as compound fertilizer at sowing. For maize, I will apply about 16 kg nitrogen per mu, with a base dressing and one ear-stage top-dressing, and about 4 kg each of phosphorus and potassium at planting. 

Water: I will irrigate the wheat three times—once before winter freeze, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The maize usually gets by on rain in summer, but I will keep the pump ready for one irrigation at the silking stage if it turns dry, which it often does in July. 

Pest control: I will spray wheat twice, once with herbicide and once with a fungicide-insecticide mix if the county station warns of aphids or rust. For maize, I will do one pre-emergence herbicide and one insecticide spray for corn borer around the big喇叭口 stage. 

I expect about 550 kg per mu of wheat and 600 kg per mu of maize if the weather cooperates. That should give me enough grain for family consumption plus a solid cash income from selling the surplus.
